title: What massage chair delivery day actually looks like
description: A 200 to 300 pound massage chair does not arrive the way a normal package does. White glove, threshold, and curbside delivery each hand you a different amount of the unboxing and placement work. What each one actually includes before you pick a shipping option.
alt_text: Diagram of the parts inside a massage chair

title: The warranty clock buyers miss: parts vs labor
description: Parts coverage on a massage chair often runs 3 to 5 years. Labor coverage, the part that pays someone to install the free part, often runs only 1 year. The gap between those two clocks is where a "free" repair quietly stops being free.

title: 5 signs your massage chair is actually a return
description: A massage chair sold as new should arrive in a sealed box with its full accessory kit. A return or RMA sticker, a missing power cable, or scuffed leather are signs a different buyer already sent this exact unit back. What to check before you sign for delivery.
alt_text: Massage chair in a living room

title: Check this before you buy a massage chair brand
description: A brand name on the box does not tell you how the company behaves after your chair breaks. A free check of its Better Business Bureau complaint record tells you a lot more: look at the complaint mix, not just the raw count, and watch for parts shipped before diagnosis or tickets closed for non-response.
alt_text: Massage chair in a home setting

title: Massage chair broke right after the warranty ended? 4 checks
description: A massage chair that fails a month after a five-year warranty ends is a common owner story. You have no contractual claim, but check when coverage actually started, find any earlier support ticket for the same symptom, ask in writing for a goodwill repair or parts at cost, and see whether your credit card extends manufacturer warranties.

title: Massage chair vs chiropractor for back pain
description: A chiropractor examines and adjusts joints. A massage chair relaxes the muscles around the spine with rollers and airbags, with no diagnosis and no adjustment. For everyday muscular back pain the two work best together. What each one does and what each one costs.
alt_text: Older woman relaxing in a massage chair under the headline: massage chair vs chiropractor for back pain

title: Fell asleep in your massage chair? Read this first
description: A massage chair session timer normally ends the program on its own, but it is software, and owners occasionally report a chair that kept running for hours. Three habits keep a nap low risk, plus what to check before you sit in a mall or airport massage chair.
alt_text: Woman asleep in a massage chair at night under the headline: fell asleep in your massage chair?

title: Massage chair or massage therapist? Who each one helps
description: A massage chair works for daily, low-effort relief you can dial down, which is why owners with arthritis and chronic pain use one every evening. A massage therapist finds and works one specific knot by hand. What each one does well and what each costs over a year.
